$comment: Justifications for every biome-ignore suppression in the repo. A suppression may only exist here, with a reason, if it genuinely cannot be avoided or Biome lacks support. Add a new entry + reason BEFORE introducing a suppression; the guard fails otherwise.

entries.why: The org logo is a raw API URL or a dicebear data URI; it can be cross-origin or runtime-generated, so next/image cannot safely optimize it.
The payments prop is a plain wire array ({method, amount}) that may contain identical rows; it is rendered read-only once the order is submitted, so there is no stable id available.
The ARIA carousel region and slide-group patterns require aria-roledescription which is only valid on generic elements; no native element fits (fieldset would impose form styling).
Active filters group uses a div for layout; there is no native element for a non-form group, so role=group keeps the grouping announceable.
Visual grouping wrappers around inputs; there is no native element for a non-form group, so role=group is applied to divs to keep grouping semantics.
Click-to-focus convenience on an inert addon wrapper; the focusable input inside is the true control and remains directly keyboard reachable.
Scrollable board region; grouping semantics come from role=group on a generic container while native DnD attributes carry card dragging.
Column sections are native pointer DnD drop targets; the interaction is drag-based and cards remain keyboard-navigable.
Generic label primitive; consumers pass htmlFor or wrap a control so the association is established at the call site, not inside the primitive.
Synthetic skeleton placeholder rows have no data identity; they never reorder or update in place and are replaced by content once loaded.
base-ui Slider identifies thumbs positionally through its component API; the array is synthetic and thumbs cannot exchange positions mid-render.
Step identity is positional by design: done/active derive from index math and onStepClick receives the index; duplicate labels are allowed by the type.
